Pat sense SOLVED 2026-07-18 (issue #80 -> PR #83, v0.37.0). THE PHYSICS: pat-vs-noise separation is 12-20x when the head is COMMANDED STILL (noise floor p99 0.07-0.11 deg, pat p90 0.85-1.90) but only 0.7-2.0x while feel-alive wanders (noise p99 3.3-4.0). Measured across ALL SIX DOF from 4 real recordings (still/wander x untouched/petted) now shipped as tests/data/pat_*.csv fixtures. REFUTED HYPOTHESES (do not re-run): (1) NOT lag — residual uncorrelated with commanded velocity (r=0.19-0.32), tail flat across speed bands; (2) NOT stale reads — 87% fresh, fresh-only tail identical; (3) NOT linearly predictable — fitted 40-tap FIR plant model removes only 1.1x; (4) NOT fixable by axis choice — roll looked ideal (20.5x still, feel-alive never commands it) but mechanical coupling drags it ~11x noisier during wander -> 2.0x. ROOT CAUSE: servo hunting while tracking a moving target; collapses to 0.07 deg floor the instant the command stops moving. FIX: stillness gate (commanded pose constant 0.5s, 0.01 deg tolerance) — a PRECONDITION not a tuning knob; ghost class structurally impossible; thresholds back to sensitive press=0.5 (blind 2.0 shipped dormant in 0.36.0). LIVE VERIFIED: 15s natural scratching -> 10 detections + 6 thoughtful gestures; 3-min hands-off soak -> ZERO. Predecessor (Fable) wrongly concluded undetectable because it only ever measured pitch/yaw on a WANDERING head. NOTE eps must stay << wander per-tick change (0.03-0.06 deg/tick at 50Hz) or the gate creeps open at wander turning points. NEXT: issue #82 expressive reactions (directional + sustained + enjoyment + enough) — key tension: a reaction that moves the head blinds the sense (ownership gate), and direction sign is discarded in pat.py:152 _classify_touch.

reachy-mini-cli pat-sense deployment trap + its resolution (2026-07-20, v0.40.0 -> v0.41.0). TRAP: a systemd drop-in can set env vars NO CODE READS YET, staying inert until a later release adds the reader — an upgrade then activates a whole tuning block at once with no config change. Here ~/.config/systemd/user/reachy-runtime.service.d/pat-sense.conf set six REACHY_PAT_* vars; v0.40.0 (af87b1d) added _pat_float_env in _compose_run_seam that reads them, and the pat reaction went silent. SYMPTOM: journalctl shows 'Pat level1!' with NO following '[SENSE stage=rule source=pat event=pat-acknowledge] fired' line. ROOT CAUSE, bisected on hardware to ONE knob: REACHY_PAT_HP_TAU 0.8 -> 0.08. tau is a high-pass time constant; at 0.08s only fast transients survive, but a pet is a SUSTAINED push lasting ~0.5-2s. The stillness gate was opening fine — the detector never saw the press. Removing that single override restored detection immediately and reproducibly. COUNTER-LESSON (cost a wasted cycle): do NOT revert the whole block to shipped defaults — it is WORSE than the bug. v0.40.0's swinging idle means the shipped still_eps=0.01 opens the gate 0.0% of the time (measured in af87b1d's own commit message), so shipped defaults leave the robot unable to feel ANYTHING. The gate loosening (still_eps=0.035 + still_hold_s=1.0) is load-bearing under the swing. Bisect one override at a time; never wholesale-revert a tuning block. METHOD that worked: diff journalctl across the pre/post-upgrade boots to spot the missing rule line, then change ONE var and have the operator pat the robot while a Monitor tails the journal. Related hardware fact: antenna sign is MIRRORED (reachy/motion/listen.py:154-157), verified by holding 'reachy move goto --antennas 12 -12' and looking — (+a,-a) draws them TOGETHER. reachy/speech/expressions.py:17-18's '+ forward for both' docstring is wrong and expressions.toml's symmetric entries are lopsided because of it (issue #89). Physical sign conventions in this repo are contradictory across files — always verify on hardware, never infer from a docstring.

reachy-mini-daemon MISREPORTS file-descriptor exhaustion as a MOTOR fault. A crash-looping client (reachy-runtime.service, Restart=on-failure/RestartSec=5) leaks descriptors in the daemon on every reconnect. At 1023/1024 open fds (default soft limit 1024, hard 500000) accept() fails with OSError [Errno 24] Too many open files, and the daemon can then no longer open the motor serial port -- at which point it reports state=error, error='Motor communication error! Check connections and power supply.' That message sends you diagnosing motors that are completely fine. Observed 2026-07-22 on spark-f8a9 with systemd restart counter at 469. DIAGNOSE: ls /proc/$(pgrep -f reachy-mini-daemon)/fd | wc -l -- if it is near 1024 this is your bug, not the hardware. Restarting the daemon clears it (fds 1023 -> 113, state -> running, motor control loop back at ~49.7 Hz with nb_error 0). FIX APPLIED on this box: ~/.config/systemd/user/reachy-daemon.service.d/10-nofile.conf with LimitNOFILE=65536. GOTCHA WITHIN THE GOTCHA: a systemd drop-in MUST carry a [Service] section header. Without it the directive is silently ignored while systemctl show -p DropInPaths STILL LISTS the file -- it looks applied but systemctl show -p LimitNOFILESoft stays 1024. Always verify with LimitNOFILESoft, never by the drop-in's presence.

ALL FOUR Reachy Mini USB devices sit behind ONE hub on ONE cable: Terminus Technology hub (1a40:0101), Pollen Robotics Reachy Mini Audio (38fb:1001), QinHeng CH340 motor serial (1a86:55d3, /dev/ttyACM0) and Microdia Arducam_12MP (0c45:636d). They therefore appear and VANISH TOGETHER -- when all four drop at once, suspect the one cable or its power, never four separate faults. Observed 2026-07-22 on spark-f8a9: the whole robot dropped off Bus 005, hardware_id went 37a38ce3a26e0727 -> null, and the daemon said 'No Reachy Mini serial port found.' The port was FLAPPING -- usb 5-1 cycled connect/disconnect 3 full times in 15 seconds. Moving the cable to a DIFFERENT physical USB socket (re-enumerated on Bus 003) made it stable immediately and stayed stable. OPERATOR'S SUSPECTED TRIGGER: physically moving/repositioning the robot strained the cable at the socket, leaving a marginal connection -- so after you move Reachy, re-check the USB before blaming software. DIAGNOSTIC TELL: zero kernel USB events (journalctl -k --since -10min | grep -i usb) means the host sees NO electrical connection at all, which distinguishes 'not plugged in / dead port' from 'plugged in but failing to enumerate' (the latter always logs an enumeration attempt or error). Knock-on effect: losing the motors crash-loops reachy-runtime.service, which is what exhausts the daemon's fds -- see the fd-exhaustion memory.

The behavior runtime's VOICE is structurally broken while the runtime is live -- NEITHER playback transport works, and this is the successor to issue #94. The runtime ACQUIRES the media session from the daemon at startup ('[SENSE stage=media source=held_client] media acquired from the daemon (was released)'), so the daemon no longer owns the speaker: SpeechActuator's SHIPPED default http route (daemon /api/media/play_sound) then times out, and returns HTTP 503 once the runtime stops (the daemon keeps media_released=true and does not reclaim the speaker; only a daemon restart resets it). The sdk alternative (REACHY_SPEECH_TRANSPORT=sdk) is no better: reachy/speech/playback.py _play_sdk calls _open_sdk_media() and opens a SECOND media client, contending with the held HeldMediaClient under the single-SDK-owner model -- because _make_speech_actuator() in reachy/cli/_commands/behavior.py constructs SpeechActuator() BARE, with no injected media_session seam. IMPORTANT CORRECTION TO #94's PREMISE: speech_act.py's docstring justifies the http default by claiming 'sdk is dead on the deployed robot' and 'the daemon already owns the speaker'. Both are now FALSE -- verified 2026-07-22 that the media client constructs fine once the daemon is healthy ('connected (default media profile, recording)'); #94 was likely always a symptom of an fd-starved daemon. A real fix needs the held media client injected into SpeechActuator rather than a transport flip. NOT filed as a GitHub issue yet (operator declined at the time).

For a 'look alive + pattable' bring-up, TOMBSTONE look-toward-sound -- this is not merely scope reduction, orienting is ACTIVELY HOSTILE to patting. The pat sense is stillness-gated and suspends while another behavior owns the head, so a head that keeps turning can never feel a pat (default_rules.toml's own note records 203 orient fires in 8 minutes against ZERO pat detections in 5). Verified working overlay on spark-f8a9 at ~/.local/state/reachy/behavior/rules.toml: enabled=false tombstones for BOTH look-toward-sound and greet-when-addressed, leaving pat-acknowledge as the only react rule, with feel-alive still running as the engine's always-on base layer (owns head/antennas/body_yaw at 50 Hz). PROVEN LIVE 2026-07-22 end to end: 'Pat level1! type=side_pat (2 presses)' -> '[SENSE stage=rule source=pat event=pat-acknowledge] fired kind=react run=pet-reaction', with a following pat 3 s later correctly 'dropped reason=cooldown' (5 s cooldown). Box had NO REACHY_PAT_* env overrides, so this is the shipped v0.41.0 tuning (still_eps 0.035, still_hold_s 1.0 s, press 1.2 deg, hp_tau 0.8) working as designed on real hardware. A tombstone entry needs only id + enabled=false; apply live with 'reachy-mini-cli behavior reload'.

2026-07-23 full camera+audio hardware check on deployed Reachy Mini (spark-f8a9). FINDINGS THAT COST TIME TO DERIVE: (1) The deployed uv tool install had NO [vision] extra, so opencv was absent and behavior/face_sense.py was PERMANENTLY QUIET since install — the only evidence is ONE line at runtime startup: "behavior: face recognition needs the [vision] extra (opencv)". Zero face events for months looked like broken hardware but was a missing package. Fix: `uv tool install --force --editable ".[daemon,vision]"` from the repo root. GOTCHA: `uv tool install` has NO `--extra` flag — extras must go inside the requirement spec string. The uv-receipt.toml then records extras=[daemon,vision] so it survives future upgrades. (2) The tool install is EDITABLE onto /home/spark/git/reachy-mini-cli, so the runtime always runs live repo code; importlib.metadata version is STALE (read 0.42.0 while running 0.43.0 code) until you reinstall. Never trust the tool-env version string to tell you what code is deployed. (3) A speaker->mic LOOPBACK TEST CANNOT WORK on this robot: AEC is on by default and audio_shape.to_mono selects AEC_CHANNEL=0, so the robot deliberately cannot hear itself. Measured loopback_rms_ratio 0.92 (mic quieter DURING playback than baseline) while a human in the room confirmed the sound was clearly audible. Do not conclude "speaker dead" from a flat loopback — use the daemon journal line `reachy_mini.media.media_server - INFO - Using ALSA device reachymini_audio_sink for playback` plus a human ear. (4) The box-local ~/.local/state/reachy/behavior/rules.toml overlay TOMBSTONES look-toward-sound and greet-when-addressed (operator request 2026-07-22, "look alive and be pattable, audio set aside"), which is why DoA orienting and the runtime voice show ZERO events — configuration, not fault. That overlay ALSO claims the http playback route 503s/times out because the runtime holds the media session — that claim is STALE/WRONG as of 2026-07-23: daemon /api/media/sounds/upload + /api/media/play_sound both return 200 and are AUDIBLE while the runtime holds media, because ALSA shares via the reachymini_audio_sink plugin device (both daemon PID and runtime PID hold /dev/snd/pcmC2D0p simultaneously). So greet-when-addressed could likely be re-enabled. (5) DoA hardware is healthy and is read straight off the daemon at GET /api/state/doa -> {angle,speech_detected}; when quiet the angle RESTS at exactly 1.0471975803375244 (pi/3), which is a no-signal default and NOT a wedged feed — orient.py latch_after_s=8.0 would call that frozen. (6) Tick overrun is chronic on this box: 77.4% of ticks exceed the 20ms budget (mean 20.72ms, worst 31ms) => effective ~48.3Hz not 50Hz. (7) Camera path verified healthy: 9/10 frames, 1280x720x3 uint8, live interframe diffs ~2.8-7.1; one GStreamer "Internal data stream error" on teardown cost the 10th frame. YuNet+SFace onnx models in ~/.local/state/reachy/models load fine under OpenCV 4.13.

OPERATOR DESIGN DECISION (Ori, 2026-07-23): in the Reachy behavior runtime a SLOW TICK IS ACCEPTABLE — work that does not fit in one 20ms tick is fine to be picked up on the next tick(s). The engine is NOT hard real-time. Consequences: (a) do NOT treat a high tick-overrun percentage as a failure metric or chase tick work under 20ms as a blocker; measured 77.4% of ticks overrunning with mean 20.72ms (0.7ms overshoot) is NORMAL OPERATION. (b) issue #97s remaining half (bring work under 20ms) is rescoped from blocker to informational apportionment, and any soak criterion (S3) that gates on per-tick budget compliance must be restated in terms of achieved cadence stability + absence of pathological spikes, else it would fail a robot behaving as intended. (c) What IS a real defect is the LOG VOLUME that reporting every overrun produces: reachy/behavior/tick_metrics.py::_log_overrun emits one senselog line per overrunning tick with no episode suppression = 39 lines/second, which buries real events and made `journalctl | grep` time out at 120s. Filed as issue #121; the fix already exists in-repo — port the #99 episode pattern from reachy/behavior/rule_engine.py (_note_suppressed / _close_episode, emit on first tick of a streak + a `suppressed N ticks` summary on release) into tick_metrics.py, while keeping an immediate report for pathological spikes (>5x budget) so the 425-1213ms startup class stays visible. Issues filed from the 2026-07-23 hardware check: #120 (missing [vision] extra silently disables a sense; add a doctor sense_extras check + a senses availability block in engine.py state.json), #121 (overrun log flood), #122 (re-enable greet-when-addressed; stale premise). Comments posted: #94 recommended for CLOSE (media-profile SDK client constructs fine now, fixed by the acquire-before-construct step in media_client.py), #97 rescoped.

#121 TICK-OVERRUN LOGGING: the fix took THREE iterations, each caught by a different gate, and the sequence is the lesson. (1) Unit-test-green version: port rule_engine _suppress/_release_suppression, close the episode on the FIRST in-budget tick. Passed its tests, FAILED LIVE — 578 summary lines in 60s, because the real regime ALTERNATES over/under budget so episodes are 3-4 ticks and each costs an entry line PLUS a summary = worse than the single line it replaced. The unit test had modelled long contiguous overrun blocks, a workload that does not occur. (2) Added close-HYSTERESIS: DEFAULT_CALM_TICKS_TO_CLOSE=50 (1s at 50Hz) consecutive in-budget ticks before closing. Live: 1155 lines/min -> exactly 0. But 0 was ALSO wrong — the engine legitimately never gets 50 calm ticks, so the episode opened at boot and never closed, leaving one line at boot and silence forever, which cannot distinguish a healthy engine from one wedged in permanent overrun (the silent-no-op class #120 was about). (3) Added a periodic CHECKPOINT while the episode is open: EVENT_OVERRUN_CHECKPOINT=overrun-ongoing every DEFAULT_CHECKPOINT_EVERY_TICKS=1500 (30s at 50Hz) carrying running count/mean/max, distinct token so grep tells still-going from ended. LIVE RESULT: 2 lines/min (1 entry + 1 checkpoint/30s) = ~60 lines per 30min vs 69696 before, a ~1160x reduction WITH observability. Note h6 said O(10) lines per 30min; actual is ~60 — the checkpoint cadence is the single knob if that matters. TRANSFERABLE LESSONS: (a) a passing unit test proves the MECHANISM, not the WORKLOAD — pin the regime you measured on real hardware; (b) when you suppress a flood, check you have not created a silence — quiet and healthy must be distinguishable from quiet and wedged.

events-cli 0.9.0 shipped 2026-07-24 and reachy-mini-cli v0.44.0 binds it. TWO lessons worth keeping.

(1) The binding needed an ADAPTER, not the one-line swap the plan and CLAUDE.md predicted. The vendor class is events_cli.EventClient (not EventsClient), and three names differ from the surface reachy/export/mqtt.py declares: is_connected vs connected, close vs disconnect, and the Last Will is a CONSTRUCTOR argument (will=/availability_topic=) with no post-construction setter, because paho requires the will registered before the session opens. reachy/export/events_client.py:EventsCliClient adapts it and DEFERS building the vendor client until connect() — the only moment the will is known. behavior.py EVENTS_CLIENT_IMPORT is an alias of that module VENDOR_IMPORT, never a second copy. Constructor is EventClient(host, port, *, client_id, keepalive, will, availability_topic, connect=True, ...); connect() fires from the constructor; publish() returns PublishResult and never raises.

(2) The mismatch was INVISIBLE to the whole test suite, because every test ran against tests/fake_events_client.py — a fake built from OUR OWN declared protocol, so it agrees with us by construction. And the publisher degrades QUIETLY by design (missing_client_members -> one named client-incompatible drop, no crash). So a wrong binding looks exactly like a quiet bus. Only a real client against a real broker can tell them apart. GENERAL RULE: when a seam degrades silently and its tests use a self-shaped fake, a live check is not optional polish — it is the only evidence the binding is right.

(3) Adding the base dep made the SUITE PUBLISH ONTO THE DEPLOYED ROBOT BROKER. _import_events_client started resolving for real, so composition tests built live clients against REACHY_MQTT_URL (default localhost:1883) and wrote synthetic ticks to reachy/events/** plus RETAINED reachy/state/* values that outlive the test process — what a late subscriber reads as the robot current pose. Fixed by tests/conftest.py _no_live_event_broker autouse guard pinning a dead loopback, the third sibling of the existing daemon-media and realtime-gateway guards. Any new outbound integration needs its conftest guard in the same pass as the dependency.

Also: five separate test files independently pin the base-dep list (test_dep_freeze, test_dependencies, test_export_decoupling, test_stash_deps, test_sleep_boundary) — one dep change costs five edits. Base deps are now numpy + harmonics-cli + events-cli; paho-mqtt enters transitively via events-cli, which IS the recorded decision, not a breach.

GOTCHA (2026-08-03, #155 arc): verifying a drift-guard test by MUTATING a source constant and reverting with git checkout can leave stale __pycache__ bytecode that Python keeps importing — the .py read 30.0 while `uv run python -c import` returned 45.0 from the same file path, and three unrelated-looking tests failed in the next full suite run. It looked exactly like a semantic merge collision between two parallel tasks and nearly caused a good merge to be reverted. The editable install (_editable_impl_*.pth) points at the source tree, so the file path in the traceback is correct and gives no hint. FIX: after any source mutation used for test verification, `find <pkg> -name __pycache__ -type d -exec rm -rf {} +` before re-running. GENERAL LESSON: when a merge produces failures that make no causal sense (files the merged branch never touched), suspect the environment before suspecting the code.
